newsitem.title: UK: Most Britons oppose idea of "Queen Camilla"-poll.
newsitem.headline: Most Britons oppose idea of "Queen Camilla"-poll.

text.p: A vast majority of Britons oppose the prospect of Camilla Parker Bowles becoming queen if she marries long-term lover Prince Charles, a public opinion poll released on Wednesday showed.
Only one in 10 people surveyed by pollsters NOP said Parker Bowles should become queen if Charles, 48, who last year divorced Princess Diana, ascends to the throne.

But 36 percent said Charles should marry Parker Bowles, 50, whenever he wanted as long as he gave up the right to become king, while 32 percent said he could marry her and be king as long as she were not made queen.
NOP surveyed 996 adults between July 25 and 27.
Another poll published on Wednesday said the vast majority of Britain's "top people" believed Charles should be able to marry whomever he liked.
That survey, carried by the Times newspaper, was conducted among cabinet ministers, leading businessmen, academics and newspaper editors.
Eighty-two percent of those polled said he should not give up his right to the throne if he were to remarry and 83 percent said he should remarry whomever he liked.
This contrasts sharply with the view of Archbishop of Canterbury George Carey, who said on Tuesday that the Church of England would be thrown into crisis if the divorced heir-to-the-throne remarried.
Carey, on a visit to Australia, said the fact that Charles had divorced Diana, 36, posed no obstacle to the throne. But the issue of remarriage was very different.
As king, Charles would become the head of the Church of England which disapproves of remarriage after a monarch's divorce. Carey is the church's spiritual leader.
